A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C. Corresponding content can be matched despite additions, restructuring, and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-classification accuracy, runtime, GPU-memory measurements, component comparisons, and preconditioner eigenvalue analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds language-model pretraining, matrix-quantization diagnostics, sensitivity experiments, and additional optimizer comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Cholesky quantization, error-feedback updates, triangular storage, inverse-root computation, and preconditioned optimization procedure. Additional model and base-optimizer experiments do not introduce a new method component; the changed momentum setting is an experimental-setting revision.

E1.justification: V2 extends evaluation from image classification to LLaMA pretraining on C4 and adds synthetic ill-conditioned matrix tests. CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet classification remain. ViT-Base on ImageNet expands model configurations within retained task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 8 adds evaluated RMSprop, RMSprop plus 32-bit Shampoo, and RMSprop plus vanilla 4-bit Shampoo comparisons. SGDM/AdamW comparison families otherwise remain. Newly cited ReLoRA, GaLore, and Wang et al.'s 4-bit Shampoo are not separately evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include LLaMA-130M/350M/1B evaluation using perplexity, bfloat16, 10K/10K/2K training steps, and effective batch size 512; ViT-Base/ImageNet training; and NRE/AE tests on synthetic and recorded preconditioners. V1 Appendix C.1 specifies error-feedback momentum 0.9 for CNNs and 0.95 for ViTs, whereas v2 C.3 specifies 0.95 throughout. This is a reported setting change, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds direct quantization-fidelity analyses on synthetic and real preconditioners (Tables 1 and 10), a toy matrix illustrating loss of positive definiteness (Table 9), a joint momentum-coefficient sensitivity sweep (Table 7), and RMSprop applicability testing (Table 8). Existing CQ/error-feedback and off-diagonal quantization comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The 100 synthetic matrices in v2 constitute a new evaluation sample, not repeated-training uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds C4, ViT-Base/ImageNet, fidelity, sensitivity, and RMSprop results. Matched ViT-Small/CIFAR-100 accuracies change from 78.21/76.50/76.76 to 77.95/77.34/77.74 for 32-bit/CQ/CQ+EF (v1 Table 1; v2 Table 3). Tiny-ImageNet CQ+EF scores change from 61.91 to 62.81 for Swin-Tiny and 57.45 to 57.51 for ViT-Small. ResNet-50 CQ+EF memory changes from 11455.2 to 11445.2 MB. CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet timing results are removed.

T1.justification: Propositions 5.1/B.2 replace the explicit lower perturbation bound with a diagonal-dominance condition for positive definiteness and add a Gershgorin-based proof, materially revising support for the eigenvalue assumption. The new proof contains a sign inconsistency in its displayed lower bound. The Frobenius-norm definition is also corrected; the principal convergence assumptions, theorems, and their proofs otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion emphasize preservation of spectral properties rather than only symmetry and positive definiteness. The conclusion extends demonstrated applicability to LLM pretraining. The central Cholesky-quantization, error-feedback, memory-efficiency, novelty, and convergence claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds spectral-fidelity and computational-cost explanations. Section 5.1 changes partial support for the eigenvalue assumption into an implementation-guarantee claim, although the added positivity criterion is conditional. The untested ImageNet-ViT limitation is replaced with boundaries involving other tasks, and Appendix C.3 acknowledges shortened LLM training.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix C.3 and Table 11 document LLaMA architecture dimensions, precision, training budgets, and gradient accumulation, alongside ViT-Base training details. Appendix C.2 specifies synthetic-matrix generation and eigenvalue ranges, and the hardware description adds the A100's 80GB capacity. Existing augmentation and memory explanations are largely relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Wang et al.'s 4-bit Shampoo, ReLoRA, GaLore, and the C4 source, and replaces the original LLaMA citation with LLaMA 2. These additions extend context and experimental provenance without substantially restructuring the related-work discussion or the claimed Cholesky-quantization novelty.

P1.justification: V2 tightens the abstract and contribution prose, converts contribution paragraphs into bullets, introduces numbered experimental subsections, and reorganizes Appendix C. The main section sequence, algorithm exposition, and much of the theoretical narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the displays: wide classification tables become compact single-column tables without timing columns, ImageNet gains ViT-Base rows, and new tables present LLM, diagnostic, ablation, and architecture information. V1 Figure 2 is removed, while its CQ comparison remains tabulated. The other figures are retained, with renumbering and relocation.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central memory-efficiency claim through C4 pretraining up to LLaMA-1B, including a 32-bit Shampoo out-of-memory case, and resolves v1's untested ImageNet-ViT limitation. Fidelity and sensitivity analyses add direct support for the mechanism. These gains outweigh the removed smaller-benchmark timings, although shortened LLM training and new inconsistencies limit confidence: Section 6.1 states a 0.73-point ViT-Base gain where Table 5 implies 2.73, and Proposition B.2's added positivity proof contains an erroneous inequality.
